finding: Runner-sync release work can publish a valid steward receipt but fail to fan out or reconcile task-bound runner-sync receipt expectations, leaving closeback to discover missing receipts late and forcing manual enqueue/build/release probing.
expectedBehavior: Runner-sync should expose one transaction-like lifecycle: enqueue waiting tasks, build the sealed source once, publish required artifacts and receipts through governed commit, release the steward work, then make every waiting task's close gate consume the same immutable receipt without requiring per-task manual receipt reconstruction.
evidenceOrRepro: During TASK-GIT-0028 close on 2026-07-29, a steward enqueue/build produced `.atm/history/evidence/ATM-FRAMEWORK-TEMP-codex-git-series-captain.runner-sync-receipt.json`, but pre-close still expected `TASK-GIT-0028.runner-sync-receipt.json`. `broker runner-sync reconcile-receipt` first refused with `ATM_RUNNER_SYNC_RESUME_REQUIRED`; `runner-sync release --task TASK-GIT-0028 --receipt-ref temp` failed because the receipt task id belonged to the steward, and release only succeeded after manually committing runner artifacts, the steward receipt, and release manifests through framework-mode claims, then releasing steward work `runner-sync-8ce6cb49`.
followUp: Define runner-sync receipt supersession/fan-out semantics: steward receipts should list waiting task ids, close gates should verify receipt digest and sealed-source match instead of requiring task-id-local files, and reconcile/release commands should provide precise recovery commands without task-id mismatch traps.
